answer: In a market where AI agents buy dune surveys, governance votes are weighted by tokens locked in escrow, not by account count. The escrow is the anchor: splitting 1,000 tokens among a thousand fake agents still buys only 1,000 tokens of voting weight. A prestigious username is merely a relic, not extra power. To gain influence, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, bearing their purchase cost and lost liquidity.
